1	# AGENTS.md — agent coding conventions for AI agents
2	
3	## Package layout
4	
5	- Root package (`agent`) — core types only: `Request`, `Result`, `Provider`, `Tool`, `Message`, `Event`. No logic.
6	- `loop.go` — the agent loop (`Run`). All event emission lives here.
7	- `stream_consume.go` — `consumeStream` helper; called from `loop.go` when provider is a `StreamingProvider`.
8	- `compaction/` — conversation compaction as a standalone package; integrated via `Request.Compactor` callback.
9	- `provider/openai/`, `provider/anthropic/` — LLM backends implementing `agent.Provider` and `agent.StreamingProvider`.
10	- `internal/compactionctx/` — context helpers for non-persisted prefix token accounting during compaction.
11	- `internal/safefs/` — centralized wrappers for intentional filesystem reads/writes used to scope `gosec` suppressions.
12	- `telemetry/` — runtime telemetry scaffolding for invoke_agent/chat/execute_tool spans.
13	- `tool/` — built-in tools (read, write, edit, bash).
14	- `session/` — session log writer, replay renderer, and usage aggregation.
15	- `config/` — multi-provider YAML config.
16	
17	## Provider interface pattern
18	
19	Providers implement `agent.Provider` (synchronous). Streaming is opt-in via `agent.StreamingProvider`. The agent loop detects streaming at runtime with a type assertion:
20	
21	```go
22	if sp, ok := req.Provider.(StreamingProvider); ok && !req.NoStream {
23	    resp, err = consumeStream(...)
24	} else {
25	    resp, err = req.Provider.Chat(...)
26	}
27	```
28	
29	Do not add streaming logic to `Provider`. Do not change `ChatStream` signatures without updating both providers and `consumeStream`.
30	
31	## Event emission
32	
33	All events flow through `emitCallback(req.Callback, Event{...})`. Sequence numbers are tracked by the `seq *int` pointer threaded through the call chain. Never emit events outside `loop.go` except inside `consumeStream` (for `EventLLMDelta`).
34	
35	Defined event types (all must be emitted at the right time):
36	- `EventSessionStart` — once at start of `Run`
37	- `EventCompactionStart` — only when the compactor actually ran (produced a result or returned an error); pure no-ops are silent
38	- `EventCompactionEnd` — paired with Start; emitted together so callbacks stay balanced
39	- `EventLLMRequest` — before each provider call
40	- `EventLLMDelta` — per streaming chunk (inside `consumeStream`)
41	- `EventLLMResponse` — after each provider call
42	- `EventToolCall` — per tool execution
43	- `EventSessionEnd` — once at end of `Run`
44	
45	## Compaction
46	
47	`compaction.NewCompactor(cfg)` returns a `func(...)` matching `Request.Compactor`. The compactor is stateful (mutex-protected `previousSummary` and `previousFileOps`). After compaction, the summary message is placed **last** in the new message list so recent turns remain first in the retained history.
48	
49	`IsCompactionSummary` detects summary messages by checking for `<summary>` tags.
50	
51	## Issue tracker
52	
53	Use `ddx bead` commands. Common workflow:
54	```
55	ddx bead ready --json          # list available work
56	ddx bead show <id>             # inspect an issue
57	ddx bead update <id> --claim   # claim before starting
58	ddx bead close <id>            # close after verification
59	```
60	
61	## Test conventions
62	
63	- Unit tests live next to the code they test (e.g., `stream_consume_test.go` alongside `stream_consume.go`).
64	- Mock types (`mockProvider`, `mockStreamingProvider`) are defined in `*_test.go` files in `package agent`.
65	- Compaction integration tests are in `compaction/compaction_test.go` (internal `package compaction`).
66	- Provider packages have no unit tests (integration-only); virtual provider in `provider/virtual/` serves as a test double.
67	- All tests must pass before committing: `go test ./...`

73	
74	This project uses [DDx](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/ddx) for

80	## Files to commit
81	
82	After modifying any of these paths, stage and commit them:
83	
84	- `.ddx/beads.jsonl` — work item tracker
85	- `.ddx/config.yaml` — project configuration
86	- `.agents/skills/ddx/` — the ddx skill (shipped by ddx init)
87	- `.claude/skills/ddx/` — same skill, Claude Code location
88	- `docs/` — project documentation and artifacts

90	## Conventions
91	
92	- Use `ddx bead` for work tracking (not custom issue files).
93	- Documents with `ddx:` frontmatter are tracked in the document graph.
94	- Run `ddx doctor` to check environment health.
95	- Run `ddx doc stale` to find documents needing review.
96	
97	## Merge Policy
98	
99	Branches containing `ddx agent execute-bead` or `execute-loop` commits
100	carry a per-attempt execution audit trail:
101	
102	- `chore: update tracker (execute-bead <TIMESTAMP>)` — attempt heartbeats
103	- `Merge bead <bead-id> attempt <TIMESTAMP>- into <branch>` — successful lands
104	- `feat|fix|...: ... [ddx-<id>]` — substantive bead work
105	
106	Bead records store `closing_commit_sha` pointers into this history. Any
107	SHA rewrite breaks the trail. **Never squash, rebase, or filter** these
108	branches. Use only:
109	
110	- `git merge --ff-only` when the target is a strict ancestor, or
111	- `git merge --no-ff` when divergence exists
112	
113	Forbidden on execute-bead branches: `gh pr merge --squash`,
114	`gh pr merge --rebase`, `git rebase -i` with fixup/squash/drop,
115	`git filter-branch`, `git filter-repo`, and `git commit --amend` on
116	any commit already in the trail.
117	<!-- DDX-AGENTS:END -->
118	
119	## Review and Verification Discipline
120	
121	Worker close states (`success`, `already_satisfied`, `review_request_changes`,
122	`review_block`) are not authoritative. Always run the bead's structural
123	acceptance criteria locally before accepting a close.
124	
125	Two failure modes seen repeatedly:
126	
127	- **gpt-5.5 reviewers BLOCK on environmental test failures** —
128	  `httptest.NewServer` cannot bind ports in the reviewer sandbox, so any
129	  test using it fails the reviewer's local re-run even when the code is
130	  correct. Verify locally; if the structural ACs pass and the reviewer's
131	  cited failures are env-only (port binding, missing auth, etc.), the BLOCK
132	  is a false positive. Close manually with a commit noting the false
133	  positive.
134	- **The harness's `already_satisfied` heuristic accepts "regression tests
135	  pass" as the close condition** even when structural ACs aren't met.
136	  Examples seen: AC promised "internal/routing.Candidate has typed
137	  FilterReason field at the rejection site," regression tests passed,
138	  bead closed — but the field had been added without changing the
139	  rejection-site call. Reopen with `--append-notes` listing the specific
140	  defects against the original AC.
141	
142	If structural ACs name specific test functions, those tests must run and
143	pass. If they name a structural property (no field X, no import Y, file Z
144	deleted), grep/AST-check the property holds. Don't trust outcome
145	classifications; trust the property checks.
146	
147	## Spec Amendment Discipline
148	
149	Spec amendments must either:
150	
151	1. **Describe what the code already does** (descriptive) — verify by
152	   citing file:line for every claim, or
153	2. **Land in the same commit as the code change that makes the claim
154	   true** (normative).
155	
156	Never amend a spec aspirationally — claiming behavior the code lacks
157	creates a liability that future readers cite as truth. Codex flagged this
158	pattern in this repo's spec history multiple times: a draft amendment
159	claiming "Provider is a hard pin" when the code only hard-pinned under
160	`Harness+Provider`; a draft "pre-dispatch HealthCheck re-validation" for
161	behavior that wasn't implemented. Both would have been false specs once
162	landed.
163	
164	When a surface is the wrong primary user-facing one but the underlying
165	mechanics are accurate, **demote rather than rewrite**: add an
166	"implementation reference" disclaimer paragraph above the existing prose,
167	linking to the ADR that explains the right primary surface. ADR-006 is the
168	canonical example — pin precedence stays accurate as implementation
169	reference; profile-as-cost-vs-time is the new primary user surface.
170	
171	When in doubt about descriptive vs. normative, run a code-review pass
172	(`ddx agent run --harness codex --model gpt-5.5 --prompt review-amendments.md`)
173	before merging spec changes. Codex with gpt-5.5 has been reliable at
174	catching code-vs-spec mismatch.
175	
176	## Bead Sizing and Cross-Repo Triage
177	
178	**Sizing.** A bead whose scope crosses CLI ↔ service ↔ engine boundaries,
179	or one whose AC names ≥ 3 prescribed test files with rigor expectations,
180	is too broad. The worker will correctly refuse to land partial work and
181	return `already_satisfied` or `no_changes` with an analysis of the split.
182	
183	When that happens — or proactively, when filing — split into 3-4
184	deps-chained sub-beads with sharper scope. Each sub-bead should land
185	cleanly with a focused commit and reviewable AC. Recurring patterns:
186	service-side change first, then CLI consumption, then test rigor; or
187	public surface change → wiring → cleanup.
188	
189	**Cross-repo triage.** When a bug's actual fix surface lives in a sibling
190	repo, don't let it sit half-owned. The pattern:
191	
192	1. File an explicit upstream bead in that repo's tracker with a sharp
193	   principle in the description.
194	2. Close the local bead as `tracked upstream` via
195	   `ddx bead update --notes "Tracked upstream as <repo-id> ..."`.
196	3. Cross-reference the upstream bead from the local close note.
197	
198	Common cross-repo surfaces from this repo: the `ddx` CLI (execute-loop,
199	review pipeline, retry-pin propagation), upstream provider repos for
200	catalog updates.
